GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2012-05-21T16:21:19Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Input Field Selection and Trackball Issues
Description: I'm trying to render an HTML form over the top of a webgl renderer instance. The problem I'm running into is that the input fields are not selectable. I can tab into them, and I can click on the submit button (and other links sitting on top of the rendered), but I can't click on them with the mouse to activate them. 

I've tried to debug my code and found that if I turn off the TrackballControls I can click into the input fields (but then I can't control my scene with the awesome built-in controls). Has anyone else come across this issue or have an idea on how to fix this issue?

Thanks!

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about HTML input fields not being selectable when overlaid on a WebGL renderer with TrackballControls enabled. This is a conceptual issue related to event handling conflicts between TrackballControls and HTML form elements. The problem can be understood and verified without needing to build or run the code. The solution would likely involve modifying event listeners or implementing a way to toggle TrackballControls when interacting with form elements. This is a common issue in web development where 3D controls interfere with standard HTML elements, and can be analyzed through code review and understanding of event propagation in browsers. No build environment is necessary to verify potential solutions to this event handling conflict.
